title: Tech News 2026 – Issue 33
content:
Updates for editors

  •  A new ChartWizard is now available on Wikimedia Commons for users interested in creating charts from their own data. The wizard makes the Chart extension more beginner-friendly by allowing editors to create charts, such as bar and pie charts, without needing to use JSON. Users can still switch to the JSON editor if they prefer. Feedback on the new tool is welcome on the wish talk page.
  •  View all 19 community-submitted tasks that were resolved last week. For example, an issue where the Wikipedia iOS app’s Picture of the Day widget displayed the same image every day instead of updating daily, has now been fixed. [1]

    • Updates for technical contributors

  • Math formula SVG images will soon be generated in the browser instead of on the server. MathML continues to be generated on the server and renders in the browser without JavaScript. Wikibooks will see this change on 12 August, Wikisource on 19 August and Wikipedia from 20-27 August. You can try this by selecting “Client side MathJax rendering (for browsers with limited MathML support)” in your preferences. This change is part of deprecating RESTBase and deprecating Mathoid. [2]
creator: Sandister Tei (WMF)

title: My GLAM Journey in Rajshahi Public Library, Bangladesh
content:
Rajshahi Public Library, Bangladesh, established in 1884, is one of the oldest libraries in Bangladesh. Over more than a century, it has collected a wide range of books. When we opened the first old books in Rajshahi Public Library for GLAM project, it was clear that numerous books were at least a century old. That was when we realized this is the best place for GLAM.

The challenge was to preserve these works without harming the original books and to make their knowledge available beyond the walls of the library. This idea led to the Wikimedia GLAM Project at Rajshahi Public Library, where I joined as a Wikimedian in Residence. The project aims to identify public domain books, digitise them carefully, and make them available through Wikimedia projects, including Wikimedia Commons and Bengali Wikisource.

title: Wikisignals.org: Helping Editors Evaluate Reference Reliability
content:
Wikipedia’s credibility relies on its sources. To help editors reliably evaluate external references, a group of us at WikiCredCon 2025 built WikiSignals.org, a searchable database of website credibility indicators. Our goal is to include the trove of reference-reliability data in Wikimedia. But their lack of structured data and accessibility is an obstacle. This is our appeal to the community for help helping you. We need the community’s assistance with four proposals:

  • Wikimedia: Create a standardized, machine-readable template for Reliable Sources pages.
  • Wikipedia: Make external-link count by website domain easy to machine-harvest.
  • Wikidata: Populate missing news-source data in Wikidata, especially from Wikipedia article Infoboxes. 
  • Wikidata: Extend the news-source related properties in Wikidata.

title: Zero-budget programs you could start tommorrow
content:
What I Learned About 3 Zero-Funding Programs You Can Do. Link of session slides (Google slides)

I’m a volunteer with the Wikimedia Tanzania community, I contribute to Wikimedia Commons, Lingua Libre, Wikidata and Swahili Wikipedia. I attended Wikimania 2026 in Paris on a Tandem Scholarship funded by Wikimedia Deutschland. As someone engaging to grow our local community, I went into this workshop curious about what’s possible without a budget at all and left with more than I expected.

There are countless knowledge gaps out there that volunteers and communities can start closing today, with the knowledge we already have. And often, that work is exactly what opens doors to bigger platforms, partnerships, and more opportunities in the movement.

Asaf Bartov’s workshop had 3 parts but I will share about two first parts.

title: OpenSpeaks Tools Update: Subtitler, Tome, and Bento Go Stable — Meet Media Dashboard
content:
Just over two months ago, we introduced three tools built by and for community language documenters: Subtitler, Tome, and Bento. They were alpha/beta then. We want to update that all three are now stable, thanks to our fellow technical contributors. We’re also introducing a fourth tool, the OpenSpeaks Media Dashboard (OMD), to help documenters see how media files are used across Wikimedia projects.

OpenSpeaks Subtitler is our flagship tool and a subtitle editor. In addition to captioning/subtitling, it can now fetch audio, video, and subtitle files from Wikimedia Commons, edit and machine-translate subtitles, and upload the subtitles back to Commons. It has gotten simpler: load a file, caption it, translate it, publish it, without leaving the tool. A side-by-side translation panel with machine-translation assistance is in place, too. Our future plan is to add a feature for automatic speech recognition (ASR)-assisted rough drafts, though ASR is still weak or absent for Indigenous and various local languages.

title: This Month at WMGH (July 2026): Localization, Wiki Loves Places Photo Walk & Wikimania 2026
content:
July for Wikimedia Ghana User Group was a month of collaboration, learning, and community participation. We localized Wikimedia features for Ghanaian language Wikipedias, took our Wiki Loves Places 2026 campaign to the streets through a photo walk, and connected with the global Wikimedia movement during Wikimania 2026.

Here’s what we’ve been up to!

On 11 July 2026, we hosted a localization workshop to translate interface messages of the Suggestion Mode feature under Edit Check for the Ghanaian Pidgin Wikipedia through Translatewiki.net.

Both new and experienced contributors learned how to translate on translatewiki and explored best practices for producing high-quality translations.

By the end of the workshop, all 110 messages for the Suggestion Mode feature had been translated into Ghanaian Pidgin. We look forward to localizing more of Wikimedia’s widely used features to make them more accessible for contributors.

Read more on Diff: Localization of Wikimedia Features: Translating Suggestion Mode for Ghanaian Language Wikipedias

title: 2025 Wikidata Research Grant Results: Driving Knowledge Graph Innovation for Legal and Enterprise Applications
content:
The 2025 Wikidata Research Grant Program, organized by Wikimedia Indonesia, has resulted in two studies demonstrating how the Wikidata ecosystem can be leveraged to address a wide range of needs, from managing Indonesian legal data to developing knowledge management systems within organizations. The two studies show that Wikidata serves not only as an open database but also as a foundation for developing knowledge graphs and enabling data interoperability.

The study LegaLi-JSON: Building a Linked Knowledge Graph of Indonesian Appellate and Supreme Court Decisions focuses on developing a structured data representation for appellate court and Supreme Court decisions in Indonesia. Until now, court decisions have generally been available in document form, making it difficult to automatically analyze relationships among cases, judges, and cited regulations.

Through this research, the team developed a JSON-based data format capable of representing decision metadata in a structured manner and linking it into a linked knowledge graph. This approach enables entities such as cases, judges, courts, and regulations to be interconnected, making them easier to explore and analyze.

title: Swimming in New Waters: My Wiki-Story
content:
I open my browser, type the word “Casa” press Enter, and wait for the page to load. This is my way of checking my connection when the internet seems to be acting up. If all goes well, the first link that appears on the screen is http://es.wikipedia.org: Casa – Wikipedia, la enciclopedia libre. Online, most searches related to knowledge lead us to Wikipedia. I’d even go so far as to say they’re all of them.

For a long time, the platform struck me as a kind of “meta-knowledge”: a complex and abstract entity, clearly beyond the capabilities of any user.

My first real encounter with this “meta-cognitive power” took place a little over three years ago. I must admit that at first it wasn’t a pleasant or smooth experience; on the contrary, I found it extremely confusing. I’m not referring to the act of consuming the content, but rather to that of creating it. My first attempt at editing showed me that I was truly facing a complex, incomprehensible system.

title: Asọmpi Okwu Narị abụọ – Igbo Wikiquote 200 Quotes Challenge
content:
The preservation of indigenous languages extends beyond spoken communication—it also requires creating accessible digital resources that document culture, history, and knowledge for future generations. With this goal in mind, the Igbo Wikimedians User Group organized the Asọmpi Okwu Narị Abụọ – Igbo Wikiquote 200 Quotes Challenge, a month-long campaign held from 2 June to 30 June 2026 to expand content on the Igbo-language Wikiquote.

The campaign encouraged community members to create at least 200 Wikiquote pages, making it one of the group’s focused efforts to increase freely accessible Igbo-language quotations on Wikimedia projects. At the same time, it served as a learning opportunity for new contributors who were interested in joining the Wikiquote community and improving their editing skills.

While Wikipedia documents encyclopedic knowledge, Wikiquote preserves the words of notable people—their speeches, memorable statements, proverbs, and expressions that have shaped society. For many indigenous languages, including Igbo, this content remains relatively limited compared to larger language communities.
